headline: Of 9 checkable claims and 3 gradeable predictions, 6 supported, 1 partially supported, 0 contradicted, 5 not-checkable; every book-value anchor provisional pending a lawful copy (H1); the globalization prediction (P2) is scored separately in 002.

metrics.label: D1 — manufacturing small-plant (<100 emp) employment share
metrics.note: plant-size reversal is manufacturing-only (mean estab size 58.7→45.8); economy-wide the opposite — Schwartz's outsourcing twist. D1 verdict cell = not-checkable (attribution)

metrics.label: C1 — Emilia-Romagna per-capita income vs Italian mean
metrics.note: supported; Eurostat PPS endpoint +19.5% vs Italy (116.8% of EU27) in 2024, reported not graded

metrics.label: B1 — durable saturation by early 1970s (1973 penetration)
metrics.note: supported; all 4 durables ≥0.93× their 1984 level by 1973 [PREVIEW-CALIBRATED]; TV from HS-42 (OWID TV starts 1992)

metrics.label: C4 — US EAF (minimill) steel share
metrics.baseline_label: USGS DS140 blocked; no OA quote staged
metrics.note: DATA TRAJECTORY, not a graded book claim; C4 anchor demoted (zero attribution sources). China 10.2% EAF / 89.8% BOF

metrics.label: Verdict tally (no pooled score)
metrics.note: structured counts over 9 claims + 3 predictions (P2 handed to study 002)

figures.caption: D1: the plant-size reversal is a manufacturing phenomenon (orange) — small-plant employment share rises and mean establishment size falls — while economy-wide (blue) the opposite holds. BDS 1978-2023; shaded = pre-1978 literature-quoted segment (Carlsson 1988).
figures.alt: Two-panel line chart; manufacturing small-establishment share rises and mean size falls, economy-wide trends opposite.

figures.caption: C1: Emilia-Romagna per-capita income relative to the Italian mean — Rinaldi historical values (+29% by 1980, 2nd place by 1995) spliced to the modern Eurostat PPS series (+19.5% in 2024). 1951 was 7th place (rank, not %).
figures.alt: Line chart of Emilia-Romagna relative income over time with a labelled splice between historical and modern sources.

figures.caption: B1: US household penetration of four consumer durables in 1973 vs 1984; all four were already at ≥93% of their 1984 level by 1973 (ratio labelled), so core durable markets were saturated by the early 1970s.
figures.alt: Grouped bar chart comparing 1973 and 1984 penetration for automobile, refrigerator, washing machine and TV.

notes: No replication score and no pooled score anywhere (R5/H4/PS-C2): this is a claims-verification scorecard for a book under GO-WITH-SCOPE, not a replication. No score field exists in the result_card or followup_summary schema, so none was nulled or worked around; the tallies above are structured verdict counts (allowed). The GO-WITH-SCOPE book has no replication_score.json/verdicts.json by design (confirmed absent).

Williams et al. (1987, Economy & Society 16(3)) audited these claims at publication; it is paywalled and was not read; our verdicts are independent of it and must be compared against it before external publication. (Gate A3: williams1987 not staged, so C4/D1 restoration events did not fire.)

Every book-value anchor is PROVISIONAL-PENDING-H1; no 'the book says p.Y' claim is made. C4, D1 and C2/C3 are demoted to not-checkable (attribution) and their data stories are reported without book attribution.
Deviation (logged): B3 uses FRED OPHNFB (nonfarm-business labor productivity, 1947+) because the named OPHMFG series starts only in 1987 and cannot reach the pre-1973 window ('or successor' clause).

C4 historical EAF has no staged supply route (USGS DS140 blocked, no OA Minerals-Yearbook quote), so only the 2024 worldsteel endpoint is computable; C2/C3 has no 1980s Eurostat backcast and no staged Italian district sector series (named next-tick item).
P2 (Exit 1 / globalization) is out of scope here and is study 002 entire.
